steps.text: There is no complicated ceremony, no tedious process to undergo.
Federico looks at the frigid information port. All it takes is a flicker of his halo to reveal an infinity of sights.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Halos can transfer this much information this quickly?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Neither medical texts nor ancient scripture have ever described this phenomenon. From antiquity, halos have only ever transferred simple emotions through the process we call empathy.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why is that?

a.text: Interaction target information handling capacity insufficient. Pre-interaction information conversion required.
Performing information conversion during interaction may cause damage to information processor of interaction target, leading to temporary and/or permanent disability.
Andoain Agathangelos is currently in this condition.

steps.text: Federico looks to his side.
Andoain is slumped to the floor in dismay, his eyes clouded. Dried rivulets of blood frame his features in a worrying manner.
For a moment, he struggles to lift his head, once more pointing his halo at the port.
And once more he feebly hangs his head.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Andoain, according to this machine—or rather, the Law—you cannot handle any further information.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And your prior overuse of Originium Arts has already had an adverse effect on your body.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are to stop attempting to access the machine immediately, before you cause permanent damage to yourself.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: More information...?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, I still haven't seen anything. I still don't know anything!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But this should not be... Why?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: These past ten years, all this suffering, all these sins... Was it all just to meet with a silent god?!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I can't stop here, Federico.
Once more, Andoain Agathangelos stubbornly raises his halo towards the machine.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: ...The child.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Is this yet another dream?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: It's not. The Law would not construct a dreamscape for you alone.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Federico chose to communicate with the Law in its own language, while you cannot understand it, nor are you willing to accept such an impersonal tongue.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: It is you who, word by word, line by line, 'translated' this language into what we see now.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If this is not a dream, then why... are you still alive?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Because you wanted me to live, Nurturer.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I set off that bomb myself... You were there.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Not only did you want me to live, you had great expectations of me.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You hoped I would live a happy life. You hoped I would break through the dome of the Shrine of Nurtury, that I would fly up and touch the sky.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You hoped to see my feathers shine in the sunlight, to see my talons clasp frolicking musbeasts.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You looked up the tallest tree in Terra on the intercity net, didn't you? You thought that, since I'm an arborbeast, I would much rather climb a real tree than comfort bells.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I did. Atop the mountains of Sami and amidst the forests of Bolívar, there are great trees straight out of legend, stouter than the Tower of Revelations, taller than the Basilica...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I really did think about bringing you to see them. On the net, I saw other arborbeasts up in the canopy crying out to the sun.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I wanted to see you cry out in carefree joy, just like them.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Hmm, where did things go wrong from there?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: When did you stop treating me as a real life?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You know, don't you?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: The funeral. My mother's funeral.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: No matter. Come with me. This time, we shall leave behind no regrets.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What do you mean? Is the funeral still going on?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: The funeral shall never end.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He is unresponsive.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Is he suffering from the same condition as the Pope?

a.text: Negative. Andoain Agathangelos is still suitable, and is currently pre-processing information.
Federico Giallo, prerequisite information synchronization complete.
Now, assist in bringing the Transfiguration to completion.

steps.text: Federico has expressed doubt, has even been shaken by past events, but he has never once questioned the Law.
After all, saints implement the Law, while executors enforce it, as is right and good.
But now, facing the Law itself, he feels only confusion.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I still have doubts.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The ultimate purpose of the Law is to grant halos to all organic and inorganic matter, this I know.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But choosing the Summit of Nations as the method of achieving this... Is this the decree of the Law?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It's far too inefficient, and its feasibility is questionable.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Summit was meant to found a Terra-wide religion, something unprecedented in the civilized history of this land. Mere proposals, negotiations and revelations of 'miracles' will be insufficient to achieve this.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Not to mention that according to the information I just received, the moment the very first Sankta received their halos, they abandoned their Teekaz mission without the slightest hesitation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If my understanding of the halo is correct, bestowing one on an individual is completely unrelated to their faith?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Summit of Nations, the Nativity... These may both be based on an unnecessary precondition.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I must confirm, what is the true nature of the halo?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And what is the Law, or rather, your self-designation of 'PCS'?

a.text: PCS: Personality and Cognition Synchronization system.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That confirms it. My understanding is correct.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Since the Law is able to synchronize personalities and knowledge—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why not simply synchronize everything directly?

a.text: First Circumstellar Habitable Zone Autonomous Technology Operation Convention—
'The synchronization or revision of personality or cognition must be initiated by the target accepting said synchronization or revision.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: 'Convention'. A form of regulation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Is the Law restricted by any other regulations?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Who established this convention? What mechanism ensures it is followed?

a.text: The ability to enforce this convention no longer exists.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A regulation that nobody can enforce is pointless.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A Law unrestricted by this regulation should be able to ignore principles and break taboos.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Which means I still require an answer. Why were halos used only for empathy before all this?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The answer I obtained earlier was that a majority of humans, rationally, are unable to withstand the direct transmission of information via halo.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But using emotion as the vector of information transfer is even more vague and inefficient, while also being greater burden on the receiver.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Is there a possibility that the issue isn't people lacking the ability to receive information, but rather...?
Federico pauses for a moment.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But rather that emotion blocks their ability to process this information?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If the Law that regulates everyone is a system, a machine... Why does He choose to retain humanity's emotions?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why... retain our humanity?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We've been walking a very long time now.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: We've only just started. Normally, a man would hope for his journey to be a little longer.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But nothing's changing as we walk.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Patience, you'll be seeing something familiar very soon.
As if in response to the arborbeast's words, a shabby cart bearing a thin coffin shudders as it passes by the side of the road, the wind playing a mournful dirge as it blows across the coffin's lid.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That coffin... I've seen it before.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A Sarkaz they called hero was buried in it.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I've told many people this story. I still remember... that he gave up his life to save everyone in town.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Even though before he did so, he was a dirty, filthy drunkard, spurned by all.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You didn't stay in that village for very long. You never knew that whenever he drank, he would go about the houses in turn, vomiting over their doors, all while never paying his debts.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Even if he had borrowed the life savings of others. People would scream things like 'moron' and 'lowlife' at him, but in his eyes, he was getting off lightly.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: When you told this story to the children, did you ever wonder why he so abruptly decided to do such a noble deed that night, a deed the likes of which he had never done before in his entire life?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I never figured out why.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Perhaps he had undergone an endless bout of inner struggle and self-questioning, or maybe it was just the urge for a bit of goodwill he couldn't shake.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: All I know is that he didn't do it to be a hero.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: He died, after all. It doesn't matter if we sing his praises, look at him with scorn, or even forget about him. None of that changes anything about him anymore.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Those only have meaning for the living.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: True. Good or bad, reputation is beyond the care of the dead.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: But isn't the process of going to your death also a part of life?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Those who do not fear death can do the most hideous things.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: During their most carefree of days, rare is the man who will stop to examine himself, for his eyes are fixated on a future filled with limitless possibility.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: But there will come a day that the fog of death ambushes him, a fog that cannot be thrown off no matter how he struggles.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: And there will come a day that he will, in exhaustion, accept the fact that the remainder of his time will be his journey to the afterlife.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: From that moment onwards, to live is to approach death.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: That rainy night, that dirty, filthy Sarkaz drunkard... When he saw that coffin atop the cart, and the figure at the town gates...

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: He knew that was his one and only chance to approach death with some dignity. To him, it was not vanity, but relief.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Perhaps so, but...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There are always people who do not look towards their deaths.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Are there? Not you, at the very least.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Otherwise, you would not value a funeral so.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You once told me in all earnestness that my mother gave the last of her strength to me. You cared if she died with love in her heart.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You went out of your way to arrange a funeral for her at the Ecclesia Requietum. You cared if she received a proper burial.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You even cared if we were feeling sad enough at her funeral.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: How could you not care about how you will face your own death?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I have my path to walk. I've never thought about when death will come for me, or how I should greet it as I follow my path.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Because you still believe your path has meaning.
A muddled bray overcomes the arborbeast's shrill voice. A sinister monster, bearing sharp horns and claws, creeps along a faraway ridge atop a mountain.
Behind it, several dozen monsters of similar physique jostle against each other, growling as they do so, restlessly following behind their leader.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This... This is that revelation!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Through the spiritual light, even the darkest stain can be cleansed. With a pious heart, even a savage monster can wade out of the mud.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: They have no halos above their heads, yet they still walk towards a future where all can be saved!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I must go! I must see what road they follow!

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: But you're about to go to the funeral with me, aren't you?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You want to make up for past regrets, right past wrongs, to look upon me as truly alive once again, to give me the happy life I deserve.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Is that not so?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But you said the funeral will never end. If it's just a momentary distraction...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I must go...

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: No need to explain yourself.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: This is how you've always been. Always losing yourself in the search, always eager to sacrifice.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: So go, go see what you're searching for truly is.
At the end of the trail of thorns, the pathfinder stumbles his way towards revelation.
But time overtakes them.
Before his eyes, the pack of fearsome monsters sprout halos and wings of light, like newborn beastlings, dazzling in their brilliance.
The pack leader no longer creeps along the ground. She stands, her jet-black skin peeling away, fluttering through the air like snowflakes.
With every step she takes, her form becomes clearer, until Andoain recognizes her from behind. It is a sight he can never forget.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: ...Keph?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That's Keph?! Why...?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Keph, a Lateran name meaning 'hollow stone' or 'stone-bound law'.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: The First Saint of Laterano, who named herself after her encounter with the Law.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: However, this ancient name she gave herself has been buried deep within the annals of history, alongside her true face.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: So the future I worked so hard to find, that future where all are saved...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Was just a past deliberately buried... It was just the road we came in on?!

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Always losing yourself in the search, always eager to sacrifice...

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: It did not stop at sacrificing yourself. You sacrificed Lemuen. You sacrificed Mostima and Fiammetta. You sacrificed your brothers and sisters of the Pathfinders. You sacrificed me.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: And all this time, you never even knew where this path paved with sacrifice led...

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: All you had was blind faith.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Tell me, Nurturer. Do you want to save everyone, or do you think only of consoling yourself?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: A similar tale to that Sarkaz drunkard, isn't it? Your so-called 'path' is merely your one and only chance to approach death with some dignity.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You think only of saving yourself.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: No matter. I can offer you even greater salvation.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Look. We've arrived at the burial ground.
However, this is not only my mother's funeral, and it's not only yours, either.
Rather, it is the funeral of all things.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: This place is kinda scary, Doctor.
You look at the figure ahead of you, not too close, yet not too far away. She calmly records all the data worth recording wherever she goes.
Occasionally, she will stop somewhere, furrowing her brow without saying a word.

options: Can you confirm the situation, Mon3tr?
Can you figure a way out, Mon3tr?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I tried to reconnect to the machine, but all the ports have been blocked.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We can infer that she still possesses some degree of control over our current predicament.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Sorry, Doctor, I'm just as confused as you are.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I followed your guidance, and checked a few potential places to slip away from... They're all no-gos.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: This is different from the dream that machine made...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Basically, we're trapped.

options: Strange thing is, she doesn't seem like she'll do anything to us.
It's like she cares more about gathering that data I can't understand.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Is there the possibility, Doctor... that she can't do anything to us—

spans.text: Is there the possibility, Doctor... that she

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Do you see these ever-changing buildings around us?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The city known as Laterano is currently experiencing dramatic upheaval, and traces of the damage it has taken will occasionally be mapped onto here.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Changes in information in reality should not be overwriting data inside Originium. This plan still has flaws.

options: So you never actually cared about the Sankta.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I see there's still a great deal of misunderstanding between us, {@nickname}.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I believe I can now answer your prior questions. The ones pertaining to the precious results we managed to obtain, alongside the shared vision pieced together by we countless many.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Right now, under my instructions, PCS is reaching its theoretical operational capacity.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: This means it is able to include even more targets in the same language system, far beyond an army or a research team... but rather, a multitude of races.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Through this, connections can be strengthened. Barriers can be broken. Differences can be eliminated.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: That's not such a bad thing. Not the Sankta, not for all life on Terra.

options: You're sounding like some kind of advocate for interracial harmony.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I can't deny that... though we would benefit as well, of course.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I didn't calibrate PCS to churn out soldiers or scientists we can order about.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Such a plan would collapse at the slightest hint of true disaster. Originium is our only solution.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Needlessly complex biological information will only serve to slow its progress, but PCS has the ability to unify the races into an integrated whole.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It can merge the countless lives of Terra into a singular race, who will pave the way for the expansion of Originium.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: As for whether this unified race can still be considered 'Sankta', I don't particularly care.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It seems PCS is rather set on this outcome, going so far as to autonomously perform many unnecessary inferences for it to come to pass.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: It should not have this degree of independence. Perhaps a side effect of the sudden increase in throughput, or an abnormality caused by its long period of disuse...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: If we have the chance, we can spend some time looking into it as a fun diversion... but not right now.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I-I... really don't think she's hiding anything, Doctor.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Hiding?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Rather than allowing you to fool around and break my samples, {@nickname}, I think it would be better if I showed you around personally, just like old times.
The woman reaches her hand out towards you.
She retracts her hand, then turns to continue onwards.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: None of this will stop, {@nickname}

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Aren't you interested to see the ultimate outcome?
She knew you would follow her.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Something's wrong, Doctor. I recorded the route we followed to come here...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: From the Shrine of Nurtury to the Tower of Revelations, then on to the Notarial Hall in Pagus Michaelion, which means the Sunset Chapel is up ahead—

options: Federico mentioned this route to me once during a chat.
It's the route the monsters are following to gather up!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: And then there's those unusual scenes of destruction around us. They keep being mapped onto here, which means the chaos in Laterano is still ongoing.

options: We've been walking alongside them in a whole different dimension.

steps.text: The moment you become cognizant of this, you see the stillness of the city begin to break. Motion blossoms across the scene in stutter-freeze frames.
Battle. Explosions. Prayer. Chanting.
You see Exusiai.
You see that hallowed monstrosity—
You cannot tell if this scene has arisen because of your presence, or if she has deigned to allow you to see it.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You should be able to clear your thoughts this way, in a safer manner.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The place you seek is ahead. The location of PCS...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: As well of the destination of the 'Sankta' pilgrims—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: The countdown has begun, {@nickname}.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Seriously, not even time for a breather?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Keep it quick, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: I'll cover you while you're reloading.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: What's with the look? We've fought together before. It's not easy to forget how you do things.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Gratias.

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: Hey, Mostima, mind explaining to me what the hell just happened?

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: I was kicking a monster's ass when I stepped in one of those weird light puddles on accident, and...

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: Stolide! My boot sprouted a halo outta nowhere!

spans.text: My boot sprouted a halo outta nowhere!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: It's one of the Shrine of Nurtury's projections. If you don't feel like being turned into stuff your brain can't even process, then stay away from it!

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: And how're we supposed to do that...?

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: It's spreading way too quick. It'll kick us out of Pagus Saint Marcel before that pack of monsters even gets here...

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: None of us can stick around to play defense at that point!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: We've stuffed the big pipe organ in the Sunset Chapel full of explosives. Our friends from Leithanien added some self-igniting enchantment on top of it.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Even if nobody's around, it should still be able to blow these freaks to kingdom come.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: The one they used to play the dirge for the city-wide memorial service?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: That's the one.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Sweet. It's had to listen to hundreds of years worth of prayers and sobbing. It's time we play it something with a bit more pep.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Let's get out of here, Patia. Our spent shells have started getting halos.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: The Tower of Revelations in Pagus Ecclesia and the Notarial Hall in Pagus Michaelion have been lost. The Sunset Chapel in Pagus Saint Marcel is the last stop before they reach the Basilica.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: If our bombs don't stop them, then we really are screwed.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hah, if Federico and Andoain were right, and the procession really is headed for the Basilica... I think it's too early to throw in the towel.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I've been a Legatus for a long time now, so I've got experience with getting places quickly.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: If we can't stop them from rushing right over, then...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Why not just remove their destination?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Look, Mostima, there's a big difference between blowing up a pipe organ and incinerating the entire Basilica!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hey, if boots and Sankta can both have halos, I don't think there's that big a difference between the organ and the Basilica.

spans.text: Hey, if boots and Sankta can both have halos, I don't think there's
big a difference between the organ and the Basilica.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Fine, you're right. Since we can't block or kill that giant monster, we can at least think of a way to make the road not exist anymore. She'll never be able to reach her destination.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You sure we're talking about the same thing here?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Let's go! Withdraw to the plaza in front of the Basilica!

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: *sniffle*... *sob*...

steps.name: Panicking Child
steps.text: Wh-What's wrong, Romya?

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: Stop crying! You're giving me a headache!

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Don't be like that, Hugo.

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: Why do we need to take care of these crybabies, Sister?

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: Can we leave Laterano? This place isn't anything like what Aurela said...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Not as nice, right?

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I think so too.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: So we should be glad we came to see for ourselves. Otherwise, how would we have known Aurela lied to us?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: We were rather lucky this time, weren't we? Once Aurela comes back, we should give her a good talking-to!

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: R-Right, Sister.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Let's continue with the story, children.

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: (Shakes head) I-I'm scared...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: No need to be afraid. Listen. We can still hear the bells, right? The bells of the holy city will protect us.

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: *sobs* ...But those sounds are so loud and scary.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Hugo, Giselle, do you hear them as well?

steps.name: Bolívarian Child & Panicking Child
steps.text: (Shake heads)
Nueda gathers the children to her side as best as she can. She takes note of the fear twisting the faces of the Sankta children, their halos flickering like mad.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: (Is it empathy? That monster's empathy, the procession's empathy, an entire city's worth of empathy...)

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: (We're so far away, and yet...)
All Nueda can do is stay silent.
She is no Sankta. What she is dealing with is not a gang of Singas mercenaries. The complex and mysterious knowledge floating around in her mind is of no use.
She cannot even say how she got to this point.

a.text: What can you do to calm the children who followed you all the way from Bolívar, to console the children who had just been plucked from a terrifying dream—
At the very least, allow them to feel a modicum of tranquility.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: East of the east of La Unidad♪

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Laterano, holy city of white♪

steps.name: Panicking Child
steps.text: Romya, i-it's a hymn...

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: Senior Nurturer taught it to us...

steps.name: Bolívarian Child
steps.text: Sister Nueda?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: You all know the words, right?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: There, the earth hides no bombs♪

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: There, the fields share wheat most bright♪
Abode of our Lord, font of parental love♪
He hears our prayers, He grants our wishes♪
All shall bask in His love♪
The K'uk'ulkan thinks back to the past. The gravely wounded nun closed herself off from the world as she sang, until pain and night melted away into her song.
The K'uk'ulkan sings once more this song she has sung a hundred thousand times before. It no longer matters who wrote it, or if the Laterano within it will answer.

She does all she can to calm her nerves so that she can sing in tune. Slowly, the voices of the children join the chorus, echoing out from the room, blending with the distant peals to form a radiant glow.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: All shall bask in His love♪
At the very least, they still have this song.
It might be of no use, but at least...
Nueda reaches under the hem of her habit, holding her axe tight.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: R-Reverend?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I can ask our blessed companions to sniff out her position.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: There was a time when, with her gun-knight armor and custom rifle, she would break the guardian gun kill record over and over. Finding her will take time.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The procession can't wait, Velliv. Focus on your work. I'll handle this myself.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: It's been ten years. I'm surprised this private frequency still works.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I wanted to ask the folks at the Notarial Hall to delete it a long time ago, but I keep forgetting. Guess I've gotten old, haha.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The real surprise is you, Aurela. Why didn't you take off your armor when you left Laterano?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Without it, how am I supposed to settle things with you... Magister?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: *sigh* You really hate me, don't you?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: It seems the saint was right. The best motivators for the errari to return to the holy city are hatred and loathing.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: So you're saying this mysterious 'Fall' that affected all of Terra brought out their bad side?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: That might be so for others, but for me... You know better than anyone else.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Naturally.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I will never forget what you did to me.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: In that nomadic monastery, you wounded me yourself, read the Curia's banishment order to me yourself... You took everything away from me, yourself.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You committed mortal sins. Your punishment was pretty light, given the circumstances.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: *sigh* I am responsible for your situation.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Aurela, your achievements earned you a commendation from the Pope himself. You were such a spirited young thing. I was convinced you would become the greatest gun-knight in history.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But all I taught you was how to control that cumbersome armor and master your complicated gun. I never helped you with your temper, so you could truly live the Lateran life.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: And in the end, you took that final step... just as I had predicted.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Hmph. Am I supposed to thank you for worrying about my character flaws?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Just because of it, you never approved of me and Amos. You even refused to come to our wedding, even though I had hoped to get your blessing.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Maybe we should have a proper talk about all this.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: One way or another, you have returned. Will you come to my side, child? My people will not refuse you, if you join the procession.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: What, want to give a sinner like me another chance in the name of Laterano?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: No, nothing so lofty.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The errari are still of Laterano. That is all.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: In a better Laterano, everyone will find their place and play their part. There will be more foundational, more profound connections between us all.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: No matter who you are, no matter what you have done, the Holy City will mend your halo and fix the flaws you were born with.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: When that time comes, all our pain and regrets will be healed in turn.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: No thanks.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Aurela...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Listen, old man—

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I hate how self-righteous you are. I hate how weak Amos was. I hate how inflexible the Curia is. I hate Laterano's stupid garbage about harmony! I hate how cold this Paradise is!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I never forgot this hate, even over ten years in Bolívar!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Even though my halo shattered, even though I was trapped in the dirt, I never once doubted that I would return!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Even when I was enthusiastic and wet-behind-the-ears, I never felt as sure of myself as I do now!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: This is my connection with Laterano! This is my faith!

spans.text: This is my connection with Laterano!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Your student turned out to be a cruel, vicious, selfish soul. Even if she hadn't fallen, she was still no angel!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Tell me, old man, this 'better Laterano' of yours, if it will let in someone who was born evil, does it deserve to be called Paradise?!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Or are you unsure about that too?!

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Question time's over.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: You've been trying to get a bead on me all this time... Failed?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You've actually gotten better since you left, Aurela—

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Grkh! *cough* *cough*—Flagritriba!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: These new glasses Vani got me... turned out really clear...
